subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, show that r₁ + r₂ + r₃ − r = 4R.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.76 — SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles, answer 84.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. Paired in the book with 84.2. Both are proved by grouping the four radii into TWO pairs and collapsing each pair with a compound-angle formula. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the same book prints 1+1+1+1 for the 4-mark answers 58 and 59 on book p.63 and 1+2+1 for answer 61 on p.64, so both shapes used in this unit are the book's own. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q17 is the Properties of Triangles slot. Together with Q24 (LAQ) this unit holds TWO slots — one of only two units to do so, Matrices being the other.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Group into two pairs
steps.margin_note: Half the marks, and the choice that makes it work. Group (r₁ + r₂) and (r₃ − r), so each pair shares a factor — 4R cos(C/2) for the first, 4R sin(C/2) for the second.

recall.must_convey: That the four radii are grouped as (r₁+r₂) and (r₃−r), with 4R cos(C/2) and 4R sin(C/2) factored out.
accept: group r one plus r two and r three minus r then take four R cos half C and four R sin half C common
pair them so each pair has a common factor
the first pair shares cos half C and the second shares sin half C
rendu pairs ga group chesi common factors teeyyali
group into two pairs and factorise

steps.why: Grouping the OTHER way — (r₁ + r₃) and (r₂ − r) — leaves no common factor. Choosing the pairs so the half-angle of C is shared is the whole skill here.
common_mistakes: Writing r₁ with cos(A/2) instead of sin(A/2).

steps.label: Apply the compound formulas
steps.margin_note: The other half. The first bracket is sin((A+B)/2) and the second cos((A+B)/2); then (A+B)/2 = 90° − C/2 converts both into C, and the two terms combine.
lines: = 4R sin((A+B)/2 + C/2)   [∵ sinX cosY + cosX sinY = sin(X+Y)]

recall.must_convey: That the brackets become sin((A+B)/2) and cos((A+B)/2), which combine to sin((A+B+C)/2) = sin90° = 1.
accept: the brackets are sin and cos of half A plus B which combine to sin of half the angle sum which is sin ninety equals one
apply the compound angle formula to get four R sin ninety
A plus B plus C over two is ninety degrees so the sine is one
sin ninety one kabatti four R vasthundi
combine to sin of half the total angle
heard_as: A plus B plus C over two

steps.why: A + B + C = 180° in any triangle, so half of it is 90° and its sine is exactly 1. That is why the answer is a clean 4R with no angles left in it.
